Comparison operators for underspecified cyclical time (mt_cyclical_free)

Source: R/compare.R
mt_cyclical_free-compare.Rd

Underspecified cyclical time (see cyclical_time()) is a magnitude within a cycle whose enclosing cycle is unknown (e.g. day_of_year(60), "day 60 of the year", with no year known) - modelled on mt_duration, not mt_cyclical. Comparing two free values is therefore mt_duration-compare's plain magnitude comparison, not mt_cyclical-compare's interval/position reduction:

  • a == b iff the two magnitudes are equal in their common chronon

  • a < b, a <= b, a > b, a >= b compare the magnitudes directly

Both operands must share a cycle (a type-compatibility tag, not a unit - see mt_cyclical-compare): comparing (say) a day-of-week-free against a day-of-year-free is an error. Differing chronons within a shared cycle are reconciled by scaling both magnitudes to their finest common chronon via chronon_cardinality() - never chronon_divmod(), which would assert that the stored number's position is measured relative to some specific enclosing cycle, a claim that is false by construction for data defined to carry no knowledge of which cycle it falls in.

Underspecified cyclical time can also be compared against located mt_cyclical: the located side reduces to its position within the cycle via its own existing, unchanged machinery (the same reduction format() and mt_cyclical-compare use), and both sides are then compared as magnitudes.

Positions are ordered linearly within one cycle (January < ... < December, with no wrapping), which sort(), order(), min(), max() and range() follow. Subtraction follows the same order: a - b between free values of the same cycle is the duration between their positions, so month_of_year(3) - month_of_year(1) is 2 months and month_of_year(1) - month_of_year(3) is -2 months (see mt_cyclical_free-arithmetic for the arithmetic rules).

Unlike mt_cyclical, this is a total order (there is no interval to compare - see mt_duration-compare), so Allen's interval algebra (%p%, %m%, ...) is not supported, matching mt_duration's own documented exclusion.

Usage

# S4 method for class 'mt_cyclical_free'
e1 == e2
# S4 method for class 'mt_cyclical_free'
e1 != e2
# S4 method for class 'mt_cyclical_free'
e1 < e2
# S4 method for class 'mt_cyclical_free'
e1 <= e2
# S4 method for class 'mt_cyclical_free'
e1 > e2
# S4 method for class 'mt_cyclical_free'
e1 >= e2

Arguments

e1, e2

mt_cyclical_free vectors sharing a cycle (or values castable to one, such as plain numeric vectors sharing the other operand's chronon), or one mt_cyclical_free and one located mt_cyclical sharing a cycle.

Value

A logical vector.
